newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mixed Australian bonds quick to take profits.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Australian bonds quick to take profits.

text.p: *Australian bonds finished mixed as the market was quick to take profits ahead of a barrage of U.S. data later on Friday and a U.S. holiday on Monday.
*Yield curve continues to find flattening trades.
Australian bonds finished mixed as the market was quick to take profits ahead of a barrage of U.S. data later today and a U.S. holiday on Monday.
The March 10-year bond futures contract also ran into heavy resistance at 92.720, a level that kept a lid on the market during offshore trading last Friday.

The market had started on a firm footing, taking its lead from late sharp rally in U.S. Treasuries in what was described as relief short-covering after the final leg of the quarterly refunding auctions was out of the way, traders said.

However, most of the positive tone was at the long end of the curve as short dated debt remained vulnerable after Thursday's strong employment report, which added to the case that official interest rates are going to remain on hold.
This caused the yield curve to flatten and the three/10-year bond futures spread shrink to 73 basis points, the lowest level since the last rate cut to 6.0 percent on December 11.

The jobs data and cautious comments on wages by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane this week saw economists reduce their expectation of a further easing to 30 percent from 35 percent last week, according to a Reuters survey.

Yield spreads widened to the dollar bloc, particularly against the Canadian debt market, which remains optimistic ahead of the forthcoming federal budget. The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread was again at 100 basis points, a level that has proved supportive this week.
